findings.title: Raw HTTPStatusError logged; message embeds full request URL
findings.problem: The hunk replaces the bounded `status=exc.response.status_code` with `exc=exc`. `str(httpx.HTTPStatusError)` is "Server error '500 ...' for url '<full request URL>'\nFor more information check: ..." — verified by constructing one. The full *arr base URL (including any embedded credentials or query params) now lands in the log line and in the web-UI log buffer. The loguru redacting sink only replaces literal strings from `collect_secrets()` (api_key, password_hash, session_secret) — it does not redact URLs or userinfo. The same file's sibling handler at line ~68 deliberately formats `f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code}"` instead of the raw exception, and triggarr/search/engine.py:29 defines `_sanitize_exc` whose docstring says: "Avoids storing raw str(exc) which may contain internal paths, URLs, or API keys that bypass the loguru redacting sink." This change moves in the opposite direction of that established convention.
findings.current_code:
logger.warning(
                    "{app}: Unexpected HTTP error: {exc}",
                    app=self._app_name,
                    exc=exc,
                )
findings.fix_hint: use the repo's existing sanitizer: exc=_sanitize_exc(exc) (or restore status=exc.response.status_code) rather than the raw exception
findings.why_it_matters: Internal *arr URLs are written to stderr and surfaced in the web UI log viewer, which is exactly the leak class the codebase's _sanitize_exc helper exists to prevent.

findings.title: Raw pydantic ValidationError logged; echoes server response body values
findings.problem: The hunk replaces the bounded `count=exc.error_count()` with `exc=exc`. `str(pydantic.ValidationError)` includes an `input_value=...` fragment for every failing field — and the validated object here is `SystemStatus.model_validate(response.json())`, i.e. the remote server's raw response body. Any unexpected field content from a misconfigured or hostile endpoint is echoed verbatim into logs and the web-UI log buffer. Verified against the real SystemStatus model: the error string carries `input_value=<value>`. triggarr/search/engine.py:43 handles the identical exception type as `f"validation error ({exc.error_count()} issues)"` — precisely the form this diff removes.
findings.current_code:
logger.warning(
                "{app}: Unexpected API response format: {exc}",
                app=self._app_name,
                exc=exc,
            )
findings.fix_hint: restore count=exc.error_count() (matching search/engine.py:43) or route through _sanitize_exc
findings.why_it_matters: Untrusted response-body content is written into logs the web UI renders, and the redacting sink cannot mask values it was never told about.

findings.problem: The diff replaces the type-based exception summary with raw `exc=exc` (full `str(exc)`) in `validate_connection`'s HTTPStatusError branch, abandoning an established, named, tested codebase convention. The established solution is `_sanitize_exc` (triggarr/search/engine.py:30-44), whose docstring states its purpose verbatim: 'Avoids storing raw str(exc) which may contain internal paths, URLs, or API keys that bypass the loguru redacting sink.' Far more than 2 existing call sites use it: triggarr/search/engine.py (lines 366, 420, 487, 541, 619, 673, 738, 798, 881, 935, 998, 1053, 1138, 1171, 1274, 1307, 1413, 1446), triggarr/search/scheduler.py (lines 228, 362, 387, 407), triggarr/web/routes.py (lines 968, 1073). It is tested under a named review ID: tests/test_tracking.py:395 `test_sanitize_exc_http_status_error` asserts `result == 'HTTP 404'` and `assert 'Not found' not in result  # raw message excluded`. Crucially, THIS SAME FILE already implements the identical policy inline 160 lines above, at triggarr/clients/base.py:71-75, for the very same exception type: `exc=(f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code}" if isinstance(exc, httpx.HTTPStatusError) else type(exc).__name__)`. The diff therefore makes base.py internally inconsistent with itself as well as with the rest of the tree. The redacting sink (triggarr/logging.py `create_redacting_sink`) only replaces exact configured secret strings; scheduler.py:401-408 documents the residual gap this convention exists to close -- `request.url` credentials carrying `?apikey=` query parameters on legacy *arr installs -- which a substring-replace sink does not catch when the key is URL-encoded or when the URL carries a credential not in the `secrets` list.

findings.fix_hint: Restore the type-based summary. Either reuse the file's own existing inline form from line 71-75, or import and call the established helper: `exc=_sanitize_exc(exc)`. If the intent was better diagnostics for non-401 HTTP errors, extend `_sanitize_exc` centrally (it already returns `f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code}"`) rather than bypassing it at one call site.

findings.problem: The `pydantic.ValidationError` branch replaces the bounded `count=exc.error_count()` summary with raw `exc=exc`. `str()` of a pydantic ValidationError renders every failing field with its `input` value inline, so this logs the actual API response payload content, not just a count -- an unbounded, uncontrolled log expansion from a remote service's response. The established solution again names this exact case: `_sanitize_exc` (triggarr/search/engine.py:42-43) returns `f"validation error ({exc.error_count()} issues)"` -- i.e. the codebase's canonical handling for ValidationError is precisely the `error_count()` form the diff deletes. Existing call sites routing ValidationError through it include triggarr/search/scheduler.py:407 and triggarr/web/routes.py:968, 1073, both of which explicitly branch on `isinstance(exc, httpx.HTTPError | pydantic.ValidationError)` to select the sanitizer. The deleted line was the direct in-file equivalent of that convention.

findings.fix_hint: Restore `count=exc.error_count()`, or call `_sanitize_exc(exc)` for consistency with scheduler.py and routes.py. If richer validation detail is genuinely wanted for debugging, gate it behind `logger.debug` rather than promoting raw payload content into a `warning` that reaches the web-UI log buffer.

findings.title: ValidationError str() embeds raw *arr response body into the web-UI log buffer
findings.problem: Logging `exc=exc` for a `pydantic.ValidationError` renders `str(exc)`, which pydantic v2 formats with an `input_value=` clause per error — i.e. the raw offending value from the *arr `/system/status` JSON response. I confirmed this empirically against the installed pydantic 2.12: `Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value=123, input_type=int]`. The previous code deliberately logged only `exc.error_count()`. This message goes to the redacting sink AND to `log_buffer` (triggarr/logging.py:72-82), which is rendered in the web UI log viewer via `log_buffer.get_recent(30)` at triggarr/web/routes.py:389 and :1199. The redacting sink only does literal string replacement of known configured secrets (triggarr/logging.py:36-42) — it cannot redact arbitrary response-body content that was never registered as a secret. A malformed or hostile upstream response is now reflected verbatim into an operator-facing UI surface. This directly reverses the `_sanitize_exc` convention established for the same exception class at triggarr/search/engine.py:42-43 (`return f"validation error ({exc.error_count()} issues)"`), whose docstring states the reason: avoid raw `str(exc)` which 'may contain internal paths, URLs, or API keys that bypass the loguru redacting sink'.
findings.current_code:
logger.warning(
    "{app}: Unexpected API response format: {exc}",
    app=self._app_name,
    exc=exc,
)
findings.fix_hint: Reuse the existing convention — log `exc.error_count()` as before, or call the established `_sanitize_exc` helper from triggarr/search/engine.py rather than interpolating the exception object.
findings.why_it_matters: Untrusted upstream response content lands unredacted in a UI-rendered log buffer, and the change silently contradicts a security control the repo added on purpose.

findings.title: HTTPStatusError str() embeds the full request URL including query string in logs
findings.problem: `str(httpx.HTTPStatusError)` is formatted as `Server error '500 Internal Server Error' for url '<full URL including query string>'` — verified empirically against the installed httpx. The prior code logged only `exc.response.status_code`. Blast radius is bounded here relative to impact-001: the *arr base URL is validated to reject `apikey=` query parameters at triggarr/models/config.py:67-87, and the API key travels in the `X-Api-Key` header (base.py:32) rather than the URL, so the configured key is not expected in this string — and if it were, `collect_secrets` (triggarr/startup.py:74-100) registers it with the redacting sink. What remains disclosed is the internal instance host/port and path, which is exactly the class of 'internal paths, URLs' the `_sanitize_exc` docstring at triggarr/search/engine.py:30-44 names as the reason not to log raw `str(exc)`. Same dual sink as impact-001: this reaches the web-UI log buffer, not only stderr. Note the sibling handler at base.py:66-76 keeps the disciplined form (`f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code}"`), so this diff makes the two handlers in one file inconsistent with each other.
findings.current_code:
logger.warning(
    "{app}: Unexpected HTTP error: {exc}",
    app=self._app_name,
    exc=exc,
)
findings.fix_hint: Restore `status=exc.response.status_code`, matching the retry handler at base.py:66-76 and `_sanitize_exc` in triggarr/search/engine.py.
findings.why_it_matters: Internal instance URLs leak into an operator-facing log surface, and the file now handles the same exception type two different ways.

findings.title: Full HTTP exceptions leak credentials embedded in configured URLs
findings.problem: A configured URL containing Basic Auth credentials is accepted by URL validation. On a non-401 HTTP failure, formatting HTTPStatusError includes that complete URL; a local reproduction with a 502 exposed `alice:proxy-secret`. collect_secrets() gathers API keys and application auth secrets, but not URL credentials, so both stderr and the UI log buffer retain the password. The previous status-code-only message avoided this exposure.
findings.why_it_matters: Both stderr and the UI log buffer retain a Basic Auth password embedded in a configured URL; collect_secrets() does not gather URL credentials, so the redacting sink cannot mask it.
findings.fix_hint: Keep logging the HTTP status code, or explicitly sanitize URL userinfo before logging. Add a regression test using a credential-bearing base URL and a 502 response that asserts neither log sink contains the password.
